Block contents:
  • One-fact lead emphasizing the BOTH-BOUNDS window (lower = date_add('month', -N, date_trunc('month', current_date)); upper = date_trunc('month', current_date) EXCLUSIVE).
  • CANONICAL SQL for N=3 with explicit bounds + HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT date_trunc('month', order_date)) = 3.
  • Why-each-piece bullets explaining that the upper bound is what excludes the current in-progress month (a customer who orders in March + April + early June but SKIPS May would silently pass without the upper bound — silent-wrong retention).
  • DO-NOT-WRITE table (3 rows): (1) lower bound only without upper bound (partial-month leak — the iter639 Q3 nuance); (2) `>= N` instead of `= N` (allows N+1 months to pass); (3) `COUNT(*) = N` instead of `COUNT(DISTINCT date_trunc('month', order_date)) = N` (counts rows not months — a customer with 2 orders in one month and 1 each in two more fails the filter despite being active every month).
  • CROSS-REFERENCES to §3 cohort retention (same DISTINCT-over-period idiom) and to the interval-overlap half-open `[lo, hi)` convention.

=== DOCS-VERIFICATION FINDINGS (BEFORE writing) ===
(1) year() / quarter() — VERIFIED at trino.io/docs/467/functions/datetime.html via WebFetch + WebSearch: `year(x) -> bigint` 'Returns the year from x'; `quarter(x) -> bigint` 'Returns the quarter of the year from x. The value ranges from 1 to 4.' Both accept date or timestamp.
(2) FILTER (WHERE ...) — VERIFIED at trino.io/docs/467/functions/aggregate.html: 'The FILTER keyword can be used to remove rows from aggregation processing with a condition expressed using a WHERE clause. This is evaluated for each row before it is used in the aggregation and is supported for all aggregate functions.' Aggregates with no input rows return NULL (per the same docs aggregate-page general rule; count/count_if/max_by/min_by/approx_distinct are the exceptions that return 0/NULL differently).
(3) NULLIF — VERIFIED at trino.io/docs/467/functions/conditional.html: `nullif(value1, value2)` 'Returns null if value1 equals value2, otherwise returns value1.' Therefore NULLIF(x, 0) returns NULL when x = 0 — the divide-by-zero guard works exactly as advertised.
(4) current_date — VERIFIED at trino.io/docs/467/functions/datetime.html: returns the current date as a DATE type at query start, no parentheses. `year(current_date)` and `date_trunc('month', current_date)` both evaluate correctly.
(5) date_add — VERIFIED: `date_add(unit, value, timestamp)` 'Adds an interval value of type unit to timestamp'. `date_add('month', -3, date_trunc('month', current_date))` evaluates to the 1st of the month 3 months back — correct lower bound.
(6) date_trunc — VERIFIED: `date_trunc(unit, x)` 'Returns x truncated to unit'. `date_trunc('month', current_date)` returns the first day of the current calendar month — the load-bearing upper-bound expression for FIX-B.
